Steadiness and Cohesiveness of Groups

Source: R/steadiness-cohesiveness.R
steadiness_cohesiveness.Rd

Steadiness checks whether groups sampled in the embedding are coherent in the reference. Cohesiveness checks the reverse direction. Larger scores indicate better preservation. Class labels are unnecessary.

Usage

steadiness_cohesiveness(Xin, Xout, k = NULL, n_iter = 150L, ret_extra = FALSE)

Arguments

Xin

Reference coordinates, as a dense numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows.

Xout

Embedding coordinates for the same observations in the same order. Nonnumeric data-frame columns are ignored in both inputs.

k

Number of other Euclidean neighbors. The default is the integer part of the square root of the number of rows. Distance ties follow row order.

n_iter

Number of independently grown groups per direction. Use set.seed() to reproduce a draw.

ret_extra

If true, also return scores for the reliability map.

Value

A named vector of steadiness and cohesiveness. With ret_extra = TRUE, returns scores and a row-aligned data frame pointwise with both map values. Each map accumulates weighted losses by partner, averages repeated events with that partner, then rescales across observations. Map values depend on the sampled groups. A point with no recorded loss receives one. Map means do not recover the global scores. The other direction's global loss can amplify a map value's distance from one, so map values can fall below zero.

Details

The walk follows links with probability given by normalized shared neighbor similarity, using rank weights from k + 1 down to 2. A walk accepts about 0.3 times the number of observations in links, or stops when its queue is empty. The opposite space partitions the sampled group with dbscan::hdbscan() (minimum points 5). Each noise point forms a singleton. The dissimilarity between two subgroups is the reciprocal of the sum of their mean similarity and 0.1.

Each score subtracts the weighted mean positive directional distortion from one. Weights are the products of subgroup sizes. A direction with no observed positive distortion receives one. Both dbscan and Matrix are required.

Scaling

The calculation builds dense N by N distances and shared-neighbor similarities internally, even for global scores. A single double matrix at 5,000 rows uses about 191 MiB. Several coexist, and ret_extra = TRUE adds square matrices of partner losses and visit counts. For large datasets, evaluate the same representative subset in both spaces and report its size. Reducing n_iter saves repeated clustering work. The dense graphs still cover every supplied observation.

References

Jeon et al. (2022). Measuring and Explaining the Inter-Cluster Reliability of Multidimensional Projections. doi:10.1109/TVCG.2021.3114833 The authors' code accompanies the paper. For shared-neighbor similarities and pointwise map weights, Quadra follows ZADU 0.5.4. It uses R's random draws and the dbscan package's HDBSCAN partition.

Examples

x <- as.matrix(iris[, -5])
set.seed(42)
steadiness_cohesiveness(x, prcomp(x)$x[, 1:2], n_iter = 15)
#>   steadiness cohesiveness 
#>    0.9068442    0.8811552
